content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I would like to understand how nesting works. The manual mentions a maximum of 58 blocks, but I'm not clear on how blocks are counted in the program. Thank you! Greetings.

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. This forum operates in English, so please use English in your future posts. Regarding your question: [product_name] restricts the nesting depth for your circuit program, allowing a maximum of 58 objects (1 input + 56 blocks + 1 output). If you exceed this limit in [product_name] Soft Comfort, the system will return an error during simulation or download. For large circuit programs, you can use signal recursion by adding a flag block at the end, connecting other blocks to its output. This lets [product_name] interpret your program as two separate ones. If no flag blocks are left, you may use an output block instead.
Ok, I will write in English.

Hi, I need help. I have a program that worked in the testbench, but when I loaded it onto the machine, it doesn't operate fully—only outputs Q1 and Q8 work correctly, while the rest of the program doesn't function as intended. I'm not sure if this issue is due to the program's nesting depth. The machine is a thermoforming unit. I've shared my program file and would appreciate any assistance.

I'm sorry, but I can't assist with this. The program is confusing, the documentation is not in a language I understand, there's no description of functions or processes, and the explanation "the machine does not work 100%" lacks detail.

Hello. Press the F2 key to generate a program report. The nesting depth is likely not the problem—signal glitches may be more relevant. I agree with the previous comment: your program is difficult to analyze. Consider reorganizing it to improve readability; this might help you identify the issue yourself. Good luck.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are confused about how to count nesting depth in [product_name] Soft Comfort and whether exceeding the nesting limit is causing issues with hardware operation. The user is uncertain if nesting depth affects outputs working correctly. Other participants explain the nesting rules and suggest that the issue most likely lies elsewhere. They note that the user's shared program is hard to analyze due to insufficient structure, organization, and documentation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects clear guidance on counting nesting depth in [product_name] Soft Comfort and whether exceeding this limit causes malfunctions. They also hope for help diagnosing why only some outputs work when deploying a complex program to the PLC.
